transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-12T15:00:00Z (UTC)
Duration: ~57 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Anand (Redwood SA), Samantha Lee (CISO, Greystone), Raj Patel (Head Infra), Avery Collins (Sec Eng), Maya Chen (Compliance)

Summary:
High-level security & compliance review focused on incident response and BCDR (RTO/RPO), uptime/SLA, and escalation processes. Customer requires US data residency, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence, fine-grained RBAC + SSO via SAML, customer-managed KMS for encryption keys, and audit logs retention/forensics. Discussed Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options for meeting requirements; agreed next steps include sharing artifacts, scheduling tabletop DR exercise, and drafting runbooks and escalation contact list.

Topics covered:
- SOC 2 / ISO artifacts and timelines
- RBAC, SSO, SAML integration and SCIM provisioning
- Audit logs: fields, retention, exportability, and tamper-evidence
- Encryption: at-rest, in-transit, customer-managed KMS/HSM options
- Incident Response: detection, classification, RTO/RPO expectations, notification windows
- BCDR: backup cadence, restore validation, RPO targets, cross-region failover
- SLA and uptime targets, credits, and measurement windows
- Escalation process and contact chain, on-call rotations and 24/7 pager

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, occasional transcription errors):
[00:00] Elena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we've got a pretty full agenda, i'll hand it off to sam to kick off with the high level reqs but quick intro from our side, marco's gonna cover the technical bits and priya will follow on architecture and private deployment options.
[00:18] Samantha: yeah thanks elena, um so i'll be brief. greystone, we're moving a couple of customer-facing features to use LLMs for doc summarization and underwriting support. key asks: SOC 2 Type II evidence, iso 27001, data must remain in US only, we need customer-managed keys, and most importantly we need clear incident response and BCDR commitments — our regulatory team is asking for RTO of 30 minutes for our critical flows and RPO close to zero for session context.
[00:45] Elena: got it, thanks, that's helpful. can i ask is this a hosted api or are you leaning dedicated/private?
[00:50] Raj: right now we're evaluating both; hosted for speed of rollout but if we can't get KMS control and the RTO guarantees we might go Dedicated or Private.
[01:10] Marco: yeah, quick note — in Hosted we offer customer key options via our KMS integrations but for full HSM/customer master keys we typically recommend Dedicated/Private where you can bring your own KMS or use an HSM in your VPC. There was a slight typo on the doc i saw earlier, it said K-V cash, but yes it's K-V cache, sorry.
[01:35] Maya: (laughs) noted. also on audit logs, we need immutable logs for at least 1 year and the ability to export to our SIEM.
[01:50] Marco: absolutely — Redwood audit logs include API request/response metadata, tokenized usage, model version, and route. We do store tamper-evident logs and offer S3 export hooks or direct SIEM forwarding. the export retention can be configured; default is 90 days for hosted but Dedicated/Private can extend to one year or longer.
[02:20] Samantha: ok but can you provide an example of the fields? we need principal, action, resource, timestamp, request_id, model_version, and an integrity hash.
[02:35] Marco: yes — we'll send a sample schema. the integrity hash is a bloob property — uh blob property — sorry, it's a SHA256 over the record and we keep checksum chaining for tamper evidence.
[02:55] Elena: noted, action item for marco to share sample log schema.

[05:10] Raj: on RTO/RPO — greystone's auditors won't accept anything above 30 minutes RTO for the critical flows. what does redwood's playbook look like for that?
[05:25] Priya: so there are a couple layers: for Hosted we have cross-region failover and automated warm standby which typically gives an RTO in the low minutes for stateless endpoints, but session-level state (KV cache) may require replication strategy. For strict RTO/RPO you want Dedicated with pinned capacity and active-active replication across two regions under Private for the tightest SLA.
[05:55] Samantha: can you quantify "low minutes"? auditors want concrete numbers.
[06:05] Priya: for stateless generation endpoints our operational SLA targets 99.95% and in practice cross-region failover tends to restore within 5-15 minutes for the control plane components. for KV cache/stateful session context, RTO depends on your chosen replication window; with continuous asynchronous replication RPO can be near zero but it's dependent on network/disk flush policies. for Guaranteed RTO 30m and RPO near-zero we recommend Dedicated active-active with regional replication and a tabletop test.
[06:45] Elena: also to mention, we provide a documented escalation ladder — page 1 is on-call eng, page 2 is SRE lead, then product ops, then account exec. we can share that contact list.

[09:00] Avery: what's the SLA credit model? if we ask for 99.95, do you provide credits or do you offer a bespoke SLA for enterprise?
[09:12] Elena: hosted baseline is 99.9, dedicated has 99.95 and with enterprise private deployments we can do custom SLAs and contractual credits for monthly availability shortfalls. we'll include the legal wording in the security package.

[12:20] Samantha: escalation — we need a 24/7 pager for Sev1 with <15 minute ack time, and phone escalation to our security on-call. is redwood able to provide that?
[12:35] Marco: yes we have 24/7 on-call rotations, our standard Sev1 ack target is 15 minutes; we'll map the contact chain and runbook. for the phone escalation we can provide direct numbers in the enterprise contract and a designated incident commander for the pilot.

[15:40] Raj: backups and BCDR — what's your backup cadence and restore validation?
[15:50] Priya: we do nightly snapshots for model artifacts and hourly incremental logs; for Dedicated/Private we can do more frequent snapshots and synchronous replication for key KV stores. we also run quarterly restore drills for dedicated customers and annual for hosted tier.
[16:15] Samantha: auditors want evidence of drills. can you share past drill reports or at least test summaries?
[16:25] Elena: we can share redacted tabletop exercise summaries and an MTR (mean time to recover) metric from the last 6 months for similar customers; action item to attach that doc.

[20:00] Maya: about encryption — we need bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and HSM-backed keys, and also proof that keys are never exported in plaintext.
[20:15] Marco: our Private option supports BYOK with HSM and customer-owned keys that never leave your KMS. Hosted supports envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via a cloud KMS integration, but HSM-backed BYOK is only in Private or Dedicated with VPC peering/HSM.
[20:40] Samantha: do you support key rotation policies and key split for dual-control?
[20:48] Marco: yes, automatic rotation policies are supported, and dual control / approval flows can be integrated through your KMS where supported. we'll include the KMS options doc.

[24:00] Samantha: audit logs retention and chain of custody — we might require 7 years for certain records. what flexibility do you have?
[24:12] Priya: that's typically achievable in Private. Hosted has storage/cost constraints but we can pipeline logs to S3 or GCS under your account for 7 year retention and lifecycle policies. we'll include export config examples.

[28:30] Raj: if there's a security incident that affects availability, what's the notification SLA?
[28:40] Elena: we commit to notification within 1 hour for Sev1 incidents via email and pager, and a post-incident report within 72 hours for initial findings, then a full RCA in 10 business days. enterprise contracts can tighten those timelines.
[29:00] Samantha: ok auditors want written escalation timelines and sample incident reports.
[29:08] Marco: we'll attach a sample incident report template and a redacted RCA.

[33:15] Avery: on forensic capability — can you provide packet level logs or request traces for regulatory investigation?
[33:26] Marco: we capture request/response metadata and will retain traces for a configurable window. packet capture is not typical, but we can provide detailed request traces and timestamps; for Private installations co-located in your network you can enable deeper packet captures under your controls.

[37:40] Samantha: how do you handle PII that might be in model inputs? we need deterministic deletion and policy to purge data on request.
[37:52] Marco: Redwood supports data retention policies and redaction tooling; for sensitive data we recommend prefix caching disabled and configure on-request purge APIs. for Private deployments we can ensure logs and model cache are on customer controlled storage which gives more deterministic deletion guarantees.

[42:10] Raj: any compliance gaps we should be aware of?
[42:18] Priya: nothing major; hosted has some constraints around HSM BYOK and extreme retention durations, otherwise SOC 2 and ISO artifacts exist. we'll flag any residual controls that require customer-side compensating controls, like network ingress rules or local SIEM forwarding.

[46:05] Elena: recap — action items: share SOC 2/ISO docs, sample logs, KMS options, SLA wording, and tabletop plan. propose pilot: dedicated capacity for critical flows with active-active across 2 regions, initial 3-month pilot, monitoring and quarterly DR drills.
[46:30] Samantha: that sounds reasonable. we'll review the docs and get back on dates for the tabletop.

[50:00] Maya: one last question — do you provide audit support during regulator review, like being deposed or providing evidence?
[50:12] Elena: we do provide engagement support for enterprise customers under an NDA; we can provide a security liaison and coordinate artifact access. legal has to sign the data access agreement.

[52:40] Raj: pricing sensitivity — if we require custom SLA and BYOK HSM, what's the delta?
[52:50] Elena: it'll be an Enterprise add-on; we'll include a dedicated capacity price sheet in the pilot proposal. typically there's a committed monthly cost plus a smaller per-request metering.

[55:30] Samantha: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[55:37] Elena: thanks, i'll close with next steps and assign action items in the calendar invite.
[55:45] Marco: i'll upload the sample logs and incident report.
[55:50] Priya: and i'll draft the DR tabletop plan.
[55:55] Samantha: bye all.

End of transcript.
